name: Orvex Thermal Shell
description:
A hard-shell rain jacket designed for the Great Lakes corridor's legendary wet seasons — the weeks in March and October when the lake pushes cold horizontal rain through every gap in the city's windbreak towers. The Orvex Thermal Shell uses a three-layer laminate membrane that is genuinely waterproof, not water-resistant. Seams are taped. The hood is helmet-compatible and adjusts with one hand. It packs into its own chest pocket.

Orvex is a Tier 3 outdoor gear brand that sells primarily to commuters and light outdoors enthusiasts. The Shell comes in muted earth tones and a few brighter safety-adjacent colors. It's unassuming and works exactly as advertised. People who spend a lot of time outside — courier cyclists, construction supervisors, field technicians — own at least one.
what_it_says: You've been rained on enough times to stop tolerating it.
story_hooks: A courier found a data chip sewn into the seam tape of a new Orvex Shell — the chip contains encrypted financial records belonging to a Tier 4 corponation executive.
A field technician's Shell is the only piece of evidence placing them at a restricted site during a corporate espionage incident.
Orvex is quietly recalling a specific production run after reports that the membrane off-gasses a compound that interferes with certain BCI models.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian hard-shell jacket with a clean, no-nonsense silhouette. Slightly boxy through the shoulders with a modest waist definition. The hood sits tall and structured, designed to accommodate augmentation ports or neural interface crowns. Overall impression: functional outdoor gear worn by someone who treats weather as an operational obstacle, not a fashion statement.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed through the torso with tapered sleeves. Generous enough to layer over thermal base layers or thin synth-wool. The cut allows freedom of movement for cyclists and field workers without excess fabric.
physical_description.primary_material: Three-layer laminate membrane composite with a durable nylon face. Water-shedding outer layer backed by moisture-wicking mid-layer and soft fleece interior.
physical_description.texture: Smooth outer shell with subtle micro-grid pattern for grip. Taped seams are visibly reinforced with thin white or black thread. Inner fleece is soft and brushed. Hood interior is slightly fuzzy for comfort against skin.
physical_description.color_scheme: Muted earth tones dominate: charcoal gray, slate, rust-brown, or warm taupe. Accent colors in safety yellow-orange or neon cyan appear on hood drawcords, zipper pulls, and inner collar tags. Some models feature reflective piping along shoulders and back yoke.
physical_description.closures: Heavy-duty YKK or Orvex-branded plastic coil zipper down the front. One-handed hood adjustment via toggle cord with magnetic cinch points. Velcro cuff closures with reinforced stitching. Chest pocket has friction-fit closure to compress jacket into itself.
distinctive_features: Helmet-compatible hood with extended rear coverage and internal stiffeners
Taped seams throughout with visible thread contrast
One-handed hood adjustment system with magnetic stops
Chest pocket large enough to contain entire folded jacket
Reinforced shoulder panels for pack strap wear
Interior zippered media pocket (Tier 3 practicality feature)
Pit zips for ventilation on the rare warm rain day
Faint Orvex branding on left chest (understated logo, no flex)
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 functional. This is working-class outdoor gear. Not aspirational. Not showing off. Honest engineering for people who need their clothes to work.
physical_description.cultural_context: Courier cyclists, construction supervisors, field technicians, weather-station operators, and lake-district commuters. Wearing this signals: 'I spend significant time outdoors in GLMZ weather and I've made peace with it.' No irony. No aesthetic pretension. Pure problem-solving.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in but well-maintained. Seams may show wear but remain functional. The jacket develops subtle creases at movement joints. Reflective piping may fade to dull silver after heavy use. The hood drawcords fray slightly at the ends. Interior fleece pills in high-contact areas. The overall look: trusted tool, not discarded.
